validity.recommendation: Change Status from 'cancelled' to 'operating'. This corridor was re-scoped and built, not abandoned -- Texas Eastern's Clarington OH -> south-central/eastern PA 'Appalachia-to-Market' (TEAM) expansion program actually went into commercial service twice in this exact corridor: the TEAM 2012 Project (FERC Docket CP11-67, pre-filing PF10-21 opened 2010, in-service effective 2012-11-01) and the follow-on TEAM 2014 Project (FERC Docket CP13-84, pre-filing PF12-19 opened 2012, in-service 2014-11-07). See status_reviews[] for the proposed field changes.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE AND CLASSIFICATION: the underlying pipe is real, FERC-certificated, gas transmission infrastructure -- not in question. What is wrong is treating it as cancelled. GEM's own dates (ShelvedYear=2010, CancelledYear=2012) line up almost exactly with real FERC milestones for TEAM 2012 (PF10-21 pre-filing NOI published 2010-08-26, 75 FR 52524; formal application 2011-02-11, FERC Docket CP11-67-000; amended 2011-06-30; EA notice 2011-09-02, 36-inch pipe through Greene/Fayette/Franklin/Adams/Fulton Counties PA plus a Bedford Compressor Station upgrade in Bedford County PA) -- but instead of ending in cancellation, a FERC 'Combined Notice of Filings' dated 2012-09-12 (77 FR, Docket CP11-67) records Texas Eastern's own 'TEAM 2012 In-Service Filing -- CP11-67 Compliance to be effective 11/1/2012.' The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', row 731) independently corroborates this from a completely different agency/dataset: 'TETCO TEAM 2012 Expansion' / Texas Eastern Transmission / Status=Completed / Completed Date 2012-10-31 / Docket CP11-67. Two independent government sources (FERC's own docket record and EIA's separately-compiled tracking dataset) agree this project reached commercial service, not cancellation, in late 2012 -- squarely on top of GEM's recorded CancelledYear. Texas Eastern did not stop there: a second FERC pre-filing (PF12-19, NOI 2012-10-15, 77 FR 62507) opened for the 'Texas Eastern and Appalachia Market Expansion Project 2014 (TEAM 2014)' -- construction/modification in PA/WV/OH/KY/TN/AL/MS -- which became Docket CP13-84 (application 2013-03-21; EA notice 2013-09-23) and, per EIA workbook row 785, also reached 'Completed' status with an in-service date of 2014-11-07. This is a textbook case of the pattern this sweep was told to test for: a project shelved/re-scoped under FERC review is not cancelled if it is later built under the docket's actual project name. GEM's row 'TEMAX Pipeline Expansion' appears to be an informal/garbled label for this TEAM program rather than a name FERC or any source actually used (searched: no FERC docket, EIA row, or press hit for the literal string 'TEMAX'). DUPLICATE CHECK: neither 'TEAM 2012'/CP11-67 nor 'TEAM 2014'/CP13-84 appears as a named pipeline/segment in the 45-row US-gas cohort roster provided for this batch, so I cannot confirm from the material given to me whether either successor is ALREADY tracked as a separate GEM PID elsewhere in the full 131-column Gas tab (outside this batch's scope). Flagging this explicitly as a cross_row_lead below rather than asserting a confirmed duplicate, since asserting 'no duplicate exists' would overreach what a 45-row roster can rule out on a 1000+ row tracker.
